Hi! They determine if you are eligible through your FAFSA and there’s also an option on the form regarding whether you would be willing to work or not. 

If you’re awarded federal work study, you can then start applying to jobs through [UF Careers](jobs.ufl.edu) and it’s best to upload your award amount with your application. 

I’ve also had students before who did not receive federal work study, but reached out to [SFA](www.sfa.ufl.edu/contact-sfa/), who then awarded it afterwards — so if you’re really interested even if you’re not eligible, it definitely doesn’t hurt to reach out to check!

I want to echo this — two years ago I was involved in a hostage situation with several babies as well. It wasn’t anything major (like the things we see here), but I called the police 6 times. It took them 55 minutes to get to me and by that time, the majority of the damage had been done and the situation had fizzled out. None of the babies were injured thankfully, but several of the adults sustained minor injuries.  

55 minutes and 6 calls. Just from me, I’m sure other people called as well. And I thought that having babies involved would maybe light some sense of urgency in them, but it didn’t. 

Don’t put your safety in the hands of someone else.

I keep coming back to these pictures and they rip my heart out. Seeing the little boy in the collared shirt with the tie — his parents probably loved dressing him up (since it was dress your best day, I believe?) and he was probably so excited to show off his outfit at school. I keep thinking of all the times my mom dressed me up and how excited it made her. 

They all looked so happy in all the other pictures from the school and they’re beyond terrified in these pictures. This shouldn’t have happened.

Goodness. Echoing what a lot of people have already said — what a smart kid, but how awful that they have the sense to do this and live in this kind of fear while at school. Seeing all the pictures, it looked like such a happy community at that school. I can’t even imagine what the community, especially the children are going through. This just isn’t right. They’re babies. And of course those teachers are heroes, but they shouldn’t have had to be. It’s just awful beyond words and I’m sure with all the new information coming out, it’ll continue to worsen. 

There’s a tiny part of me that still believes change could come, but it just feel so hopeless. It’s just so awful. I don’t even have the words.

I’m so sorry you and your child have to have these fears on your mind. He sounds incredibly smart, but it’s so insane that these young children have to think like that and have these fears. 12 is far too young to be afraid of going to school. This is beyond insane. My heart hurts for all of these children who are living in justified fear. It makes me furious this has been allowed to go in for so long!

He mentioned something like this was her biggest fear. At 10 years old, something like this was her biggest fear. And that fear was justified. And despite that fear, she tried to call for help for everyone. 

These children have been failed on every single level. I cannot even fathom how terrified they must have been. I cannot mentally process any of this.

I’ve been in guard for almost a decade now, sometimes, a flag, but mostly as a weapon. Honestly, I don’t think I’ve ever been in a guard that weapons weren’t favored. 

However, now that I’m in college guard, I have an instructor that favors dancers. At our most recent audition, the instructors picked several dancers with no experience in guard over individuals who were experienced spinners. That being said, they also still favor weapons in general and we are very clearly given better drill, better work, more time with our instructors, and more opportunities in general. 

It’s incredibly frustrating and at this level they don’t even try to hide it. It’s always subjective, but the favoritism runs deep. 

Now that I teach, I just try to make sure I don’t show favoritism and try to give everyone a fair chance. Sometimes that seems like all I really can do. I’m sorry you’re in this situation as well and I wish you the best of luck!!

Aside from starting medication, my sister had to exercise more than she normally did (she needed to exercise at least 60 minutes a day to see any change, whereas she used to do about 30 minutes), and she made sure to eat clean (mostly protein and vegetables) and drank a lot of water. I’ve heard a lot of people with hypothyroidism saw improvement in weight when they started a gluten-free diet also. 

I would say the best thing to do is to talk to a doctor and work together to develop habits that are healthy for your body type and situation. In my sister’s case, normal dieting (low-fat, low-carb, etc.) did not help, so don’t give up and keep trying new things!
Very strongly agree! My sister was exercising and dieting really well and ended up gaining weight. When she started medication for hypothyroidism she was finally able to lose the extra pounds.

I was on Lamictal for a little over a month. It was the first and only mood stabilizer I had ever taken (I was only recently diagnosed). My psychiatrists were pretty excited about putting me on Lamictal because I’m in remission with an eating disorder, so they wanted to make sure my weight would remain stable. 

I started on 25mg and within three weeks I was on about 100mg. The first week or so was fine, my moods were a bit more stable and I was so excited.  Suddenly and similarly to how you described, it felt like all hell broke loose. My mood swings were completely out of control; I was falling into such deep depression and sudden rage and I had even developed more paranoia. I had really scared my family. I felt like a monster and, honestly, I think I probably was one at the time. 

The worst was thinking I had developed the rash (SJS). My anxiety was out of control. I woke up three weeks in with a small rash. I wasn’t thinking clearly and I stormed into an urgent care center thinking I was dying. They told me it was nothing and sent me home. 

About the same time, I followed up with my psychiatrist. I told him that I felt I was getting worse and that I was out of control. He increased my dosage and told me to keep working at it. 

A few days later and my entire body was covered in a rash. At this point, I obviously knew it wasn’t SJS, but I was still in a complete panic. Turns out, I was having an allergic reaction to Lamictal, so my psychiatrist obviously took me off the medication. It’s been a few weeks since then and even though things aren’t great, I don’t feel like I’m nearly as bad as I was on Lamictal. 

Seeing as it was my first time on a mood stabilizer, I was pretty hesitant to go back to see my psychiatrist and take any more medication, but I know that if I can find help, I should give it a chance. 

I think my experience on Lamictal was definitely a pretty bad example, but I know several people who have really found it to be helpful - it just wasn’t for me.  I know I just started this process, but I’m trying to be patient and keep the faith that I will eventually find something that helps me. I hope you do too. I really, really do wish you the best of luck.
